assessment.report:
# Project rules implementation preflight

The user approved adding a target-project AGENTS.md lifecycle and explicitly requested implementation. This approval covers kit source changes, not writes to other projects, global instructions/configuration, installation, commits or push. Existing kit architecture and source layout are retained; no source restructuring or OpenSpec adoption applies. No active applicable PRD was discovered in the bounded configured documentation inventory.

Inspected root repository instructions, full README language pair, release policy, architecture and relevant shared execution, routing, documentation, blueprint, TDD/test/comment contracts. Reviewed current documentation runtime and package discovery entrypoints. Other inventoried previous design and verification records concern independent older capabilities; they remain untouched and are not re-certified. This review does not assert those records were fully read or whole-project readiness.

Approved module boundary: a thin team-project-rules Skill and one canonical project-rules reference reuse the existing Explorer/Docs/Lead roles. A read-only helper inspects the bounded root-to-working-directory instruction candidate chain; it reports selected/empty/shadowed/absent sources and byte-bound warnings, never live loading, policy permission, commands or target writes. Existing documentation inventory includes root override and preserves schema1 while policy2 invalidates older reviews intentionally. Candidate sources including absent ones become selected review dependencies; no circular governance dependencies or automatic marker reset.

Production ownership: Backend owns helper, documentation runtime and scoped package validator; Docs owns new Skill/canonical rules, listed workflow routes/profile developer instructions, architecture/folder/release/public documents; Tester owns focused isolated tests and canonical active packet. All selected named roles are available in the active tool catalog; actual calls used team-tester, team-backend-engineer and team-docs-maintainer. Reviewer will be selected independently after a coherent pass. Models are not independently reported; source/tool profiles are not loaded identity proof. No overlap, no children orchestrating other agents. Planned fourth thread is a read-only review of integrated outputs, with no production ownership; Lead integrates and delegates fixes to original owners.

Sufficiency recommendation: ready for the approved scoped implementation after the separate Tester packet/Red gates are satisfied. First target-file creation/policy changes require actual user approval; scoped factual upkeep may follow existing bounded authority. Refusal preserves originals and independent authorized work. Ambiguity requires a user decision without automatic conflict resolution or permission expansion.

Verification: programmatic isolated helper behavior and negative path/nonmutation checks first; then documentation freshness/compatibility, package discovery mutation checks, isolated fake-home distribution/deployment, canonical packet validation, both required bilingual commands and complete-pair semantic review. Independent forward use of the new Skill examines raw case inputs without provided expected answers. Actual Codex loading/user acceptance remains manual pending. No paid/network test operations or real install are authorized.

Tester preimplementation packet was read completely; coverage spans deterministic helper safety, governance/package regressions and explicit pending real-session authorization/refusal/maintenance E2E. Existing governance index mismatch was traced to Git CRLF conversion: LF-normalized content exactly matched the stored original SHA256. Only its original line endings were restored, with no semantic or authority change; old review hashes were not rewritten.
